title: Doubt of grace marks weak faith, yet does not cast one out of the number of true believers
source_text: XVII. Porro quamvis fideles de propria gratia & remissione peccatorum suorum, sine aliqua culpa dubitare non possint, attamen de vere fidelium numero excludendi non sunt quicunque ea de re non sunt omnino certi. Istud enim argumentum est fidei infirmae atque languidae, non vero fidei nullius. Nam prout fides est major vel minor, firmior vel infirmior: ita quoque certiorem vel minus firmam, eo etiam nos reddit de Dei gratia magis, vel minus certos, nosque de ea magis, vel minus dubitare sinit.
pass_a_gloss: Further, although believers cannot without some fault doubt concerning their own grace and the remission of their sins, yet whoever are not altogether certain of that matter are not to be excluded from the number of true believers. For that is an argument of weak and languid faith, not of no faith at all. For according as faith is greater or lesser, firmer or weaker, so also it renders us more or less certain of God’s grace, and allows us to doubt of it more or less.
pass_b_english: Some doubt of one’s grace is a fault of weak faith, not proof of unbelief.
Certainty scales with the strength of faith.

choices.why: Degrees of faith vs presence of faith.
